25.original: Present the heirloom ring to the wistful woman.

48.original: Would you mind giving me a hand? I'm trying to find my ring. I think I must've lost it trying to escape during the attack.

49.original: It's a plain band set with a black stone. Nothing fancy, but it's important to me─we've had it in our family for generations.

50.original: Before the raid, I was doing some shopping in the Nexus Arcade, so I figure it's around here someplace. Thing is, there's too much ground to cover alone...

51.original: Could I trouble you to search north of the arcade? You'd be doing me a huge favor. I'll keep looking around here. Let me know if you find anything.

52.original: Do me a favor and search the north side of the arcade, okay? I'd really appreciate it.

53.original: No luck here, I'm afraid. Did you fare any better?

54.original: Oh, this is it, no mistake! Thank you so much!

55.original: I guess I should tell you a little more about the ring after you went to all that trouble. Hundreds of years ago there was a terrible war we know as the Storm Surge. One of my ancestors─a scientist─had it made as an engagement ring.

56.original: The little black stone? That's raw electrope ore. Apparently, they snuck a small chunk out of the laboratory they were working at to use for the ring.

57.original: Back then, electrope ore was worth a small fortune. A gesture like that would've been a surefire way to anyone's heart─well, according to my mother at least.

58.original: Of course, these days electrope is more readily attainable, and without any circuits printed on it, a gem like this is nothing more than a bit of lightning-aspected rock.

59.original: Still, every time I look at it, I can't help but wonder about my ancestors and the lives they led. I suppose I'll never find out whether the ring was enough to send sparks flying, or if they were wed when all was said and done.

60.original: Thanks again for your help. I'll try and be more careful next time I'm fleeing murderous mechanical soldiers...
